info.title: FSH Labs ordering API for AI agents
info.summary: Price a laser-cut part from a DXF or SVG and hand a person a link to pay. No account, no API key.
info.description: Everything here is open: no signup, no key, no install. An agent checks the catalog, prices a file, and makes a payment link the person opens to pay by card. Human-readable docs: https://www.fshlabs.com/agents. The same operations are MCP tools at https://www.fshlabs.com/mcp.

get.summary: Materials, limits, lead time and policies
get.description: What FSH Labs laser cuts, in which materials and thicknesses, the size limits, the order minimum, the lead time and the codes a quote can come back with. Start here.

design_rules.description: What to draw to. Use these when you make or check the file yourself.

kerf_in.description: Width of material the beam burns away along a cut. Holes come out that much larger and outside edges that much smaller than drawn.

sheet_thickness.description: How far a real sheet strays from its listed thickness, by material family

lead_time_business_days.description: Counted from payment for cut parts, and from proof approval for personalized products

in_time.description: Whether an order paid today is ready before the holiday

default.description: The request was refused. `error.code` says why.

post.description: Prices one cut file in one material at one quantity, with the same engine the website charges from. Answers with the price, the same job at other quantities (price_breaks), the lead time, the part sizes we read, and any issues with the file. Send compare_materials to price it in other materials in the same call, and ship_zip to add shipping and the total before tax. A file that can't be priced instantly still answers 200, with priceable false and the reasons. Nothing is stored against a person and nothing is charged. Also available as GET with the same fields as query parameters (file_url or file_id only).

post.summary: Make a payment link for the person
post.description: Saves the priced job as an unpaid order and answers with a pay link for the person. Prices hold for 30 days. They open the link, check the order and pay by card on Stripe; address, phone and sales tax are handled there. Nothing is made, and nobody is charged, until they pay. Takes the same file and options as the quote, so quote first and pass its file_id. With kind laser-template or personalize it orders a template part or a personalized product instead, from the same fields quote_template or quote_product took. For several things in one order (one pay link, one order minimum, one parcel), send `items` instead of one thing's own fields: price the set first with quote_order.

post.summary: Price several things as one order
post.description: Prices a list of things as one order: each item at its own quantity, ONE order minimum for the lot, and ONE parcel to one ZIP. Send up to 20 items; each is a file you already quoted (by file_id), a template part or a personalized product, with its own material and quantity. The answer says what the whole order costs and what it saves against ordering each item alone. Nothing is stored. To change the order, change the list and call again; when the person is happy, send the same items to create_order.

template.description: A template slug from list_templates, e.g. mounting-plate

values.description: The template's parameters by key. Lengths are in inches; a toggle is 1 or 0; a choice is one of its option values. Any left out take the template's default.

variant.description: A variant slug (a colour or size) from list_products. Left out, the first is used; the answer says which.

text.description: The text to put on it: up to 3 lines of 40 characters, as an array or one string with line breaks

font.description: A font key from the product's fonts in list_products. Left out, the first is used.

names.description: A different name on each piece, one per piece, for products with takes_names. `text` is then the first name.

notes.description: Anything the shop should know. A person reads it before making the order.

file_id.description: A file sent in an earlier call (every quote answers with one). Kept 30 days.

ship_zip.description: The 5-digit US ZIP it would ship to. Given, the answer adds what shipping costs and the total before sales tax, so the person sees the whole price before an order is made.

parts_cents.description: This item's goods. The order minimum is on the order, not on an item

needs_proof.description: false: made exactly as ordered, with no proof. true: the shop emails a proof to approve first

minimum_top_up_cents.description: Added once when the whole order comes to less than the order minimum; 0 otherwise

saved_vs_separate_cents.description: What one order saves in order minimums against ordering each item on its own. Shipping once instead of several times saves more, and is not counted here

shipping.description: What shipping costs to ship_zip. Null when no ship_zip was sent, or the order is pickup only.

transit_business_days.description: The carrier's estimate, after the order is made

rate.description: carrier: the live rate to this ZIP. flat: our flat rate, used when the carrier gives none

total_before_tax.description: Price plus shipping, before sales tax. Null without ship_zip.

needs_proof.description: Whether anything on the order waits for a proof before it is made

proof_items.description: Which items get a proof, as positions in items (0 is the first)

pickup_only.description: True when an item is too big for a parcel: the whole order is then pickup only

lead_time.description: One lead time for the order: its slowest item's. Everything leaves together

default.description: The request was refused. `error.code` says why.

message.description: Plain words, fit to show the person.

human_url.description: Where the person can do this on the website instead.
